correctness.rationale: This PASS is for the replacement files under /workspace/repairs/3, not the original proof. Frozen RESULT.md Step 3 claims only certain overlapping C windows can coexist and that all other overlaps force incompatible partners; (1 4)(2 3) is a compatible joint B and C^- occurrence using the same transposition (2 3). It has positive probability in the finite fixed-count model, and its contribution to E[B_n C_n^-] cannot be dropped by incompatibility. In the corrected proof, an overlap of compatible matching motifs always shares an entire transposition. A connected cluster of matching motifs forms a connected graph of prescribed edges linked by C motifs; knowing one edge leaves at most finitely many choices for each successive edge along a spanning tree (endpoints differ in absolute value by one in the two intervals). Thus r-edge clusters have O(n²) placements, or O(n) if a B forces the root edge to be adjacent. Distinct C motifs cannot have exactly the same two transpositions, since the four ordered endpoints determine the only possible two disjoint adjacent intervals and the pairing. Hence overlapping C-only clusters have r≥3, and mixed B/C clusters have r≥2. Each is negligible by the O(n^-r) prescription bound; distinct B's cannot overlap compatibly. A-only connected sets of q≥3 consecutive fixed sites contribute O(n^(1−q/2)); A cannot coexist at a shared site with a matched vertex. For finitely many selection patterns multiply the placement bounds and apply the probability bound to the union, not an independence assumption. The disjoint leading counts are n^(a+b+2c+2d)/2^(c+d), with a one-power loss for the placements intersecting distinct intervals; the joint prescription probability (f)_s ∏_{j<r}(m−2j)/(n)_(s+2r) gives the required constants, including the α=0 cases. The factorial moments determine the independent Poisson limit. E has mean fm/[n(n−1)]=O(n^-1/2); the exact bond decomposition and integer continuity interval give the deficit and zero probabilities. The four exact means follow from the same prescription formula and candidate counts, with impossible small-n or empty-matching terms zero. The unrestricted ratio comparison traverses order √n ratios bounded away from one outside an inner band, and the conditional subsequence argument establishes mixing. Separate exact brute force over all permutations up to n=8 filtered by π²=id used deletion ranks v−1{v>π(i)}, independent direct bond classification, and rational sums by f; all 1,115 involutions matched the identity and mean. The nested four-site B/C^- overlap appeared at n=4 and in all tested n=4…8 (counts 1,2,6,16,49). Frozen verifier and logs were inspected, not executed; neither small check establishes joint asymptotic independence. The replacement REVIEW.md also removes the misleading suggestion of source reconstruction: the event is only distinct outputs for a given source.

evidence: The indexed Fibonacci-cube mobility record reports an unrestricted Poisson(2) legal adjacent-position-swap limit. Adjacent composition is still an involution exactly if its transposition commutes with π, hence the swap count is exactly A_n+B_n. This covers the corresponding summed marginal at α=1, not the full result.
The compound deficit weights each C mechanism twice; its law depends on the matching motifs jointly and with A_n+B_n. It does not follow from the known separate marginals.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: There is direct overlap with the unrestricted A+B marginal and with two f=0 C marginals; these are excluded from the distinctive contribution. Conditioned four-way independence including α≠1, plus the weighted deletion deficit and e^-3 full-diversity conclusion, need the joint overlap estimates or an equivalent stronger theorem. No such stronger statement was identified in accessible material.

evidence: Full deletion diversity equals absence of bonds, i.e. absence of both positive and negative adjacent successions (the ordinary king-permutation restriction applied to involutions, not circular adjacency).

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The general identity gives the correct alternative formulation but does not assign probabilities for the involution law. General uniform-permutation or cylinder counts and one-sign successions do not supply the mixed law of the four mechanisms.

value.rationale: The corrected theorem addresses a natural restricted-source deletion question, and explains both why the deficit is compound Poisson (paired matching mechanisms) and how fixed sites add a separate contribution at the square-root scale. It separates a joint limit from known marginals and quantifies the probability of distinct deletion outputs under two natural sampling laws. It does not assert unique reconstruction from an output.
